stem: A cut in a TV's price lifts soundbar sales strongly: the cross-price elasticity of soundbars with respect to the TV's price is -0.9. An analyst assumes a soundbar price cut will lift TV sales just as strongly. Why is that risky?

options.text: Cross effects need not match: few buy a TV for a cheaper soundbar
It is not risky: cross-price elasticities are the same in both directions
A soundbar cut will lower TV sales, since the two are substitutes
Cross-price elasticity only exists for substitutes, not complements
